title: TMA tile loads and warp specialization
question: Can changing tile loading reduce instruction overhead without changing attention arithmetic?
workload: loom-private/multisensor-attention, optimized variant: 25,000 queries over 250,000 context tokens, 64 query rows per block, 1,024-key tiles, two shared buffers, 12 context splits

cases.name: control
cases.description: applications/loom_private/attention/attention_optimized.cu unchanged: double-buffered cp.async tiles (16-byte copies by all 256 threads), block barriers before and after each tile

cases.name: tma
cases.description: attention_tma.cu, mode 1: thread 0 issues one cp.async.bulk per tile; all threads wait on the tile's mbarrier; a block barrier after each tile guards reuse

cases.name: tma_producer
cases.description: attention_tma.cu, mode 2: a ninth warp issues the bulk copies; compute warps wait on full mbarriers and release empty mbarriers; no block barrier inside the stream; two blocks per SM kept with __launch_bounds__(288, 2)
